newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks end lower on Hansol, Yu Sung woes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks end lower on Hansol, Yu Sung woes.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed sharply lower on Wednesday due to corporate woes rekindled by a textile maker's debt default and a negative newspaper report on the Hansol Group, brokers said.
The composite index closed 1.78 percent, or 12.47 points, lower at 689.10.
Seven listed Hansol affiliates fell sharply on the Chosun Ilbo report that the group had managed a seven billion won fund on behalf of an associate of President Kim Young-sam's son.
The 16th-ranked Hansol Group issued a vaguely-worded statement that appeared to deny the report but investors continued to dump Hansol shares.
Trading in Yu Sung, which on Tuesday defaulted on 227 million won worth of promissory notes, will resume on Thursday after a one-day suspension.
"News on Hansol and Yu Sung hit the market, already faced with slowing foreign buying and a slow growth in customer deposits," said Chae Chi-bum, an analyst at Daishin Economic Research Institute.
The Hansol Group's flagship Halsol Paper fell 1,700 won to its daily limit of 19,600. Among the group's six other affiliates, Hansol Electron also went limit-down to 22,400 won by falling 1,900.

Yu Sung's trouble renewed concerns about corporate financial positions and hit the troubled Jinro Group's affiliates. Jinro Ltd fell 480 won to 5,970 and Jinro General Foods closed 40 won lower at 3,810.

The Jinro Group has said it would sell some of its property and affiliates to raise cash to pay back its debt. The group said it wants to generate some 1.2 trillion won by the end of next year, but no progress has yet been announced.
OB Brewery and its sister firm Doo San Beverage closed limit-down after OB Brewery announced on Tuesday a plan to absorb Doo San in October.
OB Brewery, the nation's biggest beer maker, fell 2,400 won to 28,600 and Doo San by 2,700 won to 32,000.

Taeil Media and Shinhan Bank bucked the overall market's weakness by rising on unrelated news. Taeil, which announced the development of a new engine for office machines, closed 900 won higher at 16,000.
Shinhan closed up 100 won to 10,400. The Securities Supervisory Board said on Wednesday an additional 3.13 million of Shinhan's shares would become available for foreign investment from Friday.
The announcement came after the market closed, but brokers said similar rumours have already circulated.
Blue chips fell as institutions, which heavily sold shares on May 2 when the foreign ownership limit was raised to 23 percent from 20 percent, were taking time before restructuring their portfolios.
Investors ignored the Bank of Korea's announcement that the nation's foreign exchange reserves rose to $29.83 billion at the end of April from $29.15 billion in March.
The index futures June contracts fell 1.80 points to 68.20 and the underlying KOSPI-200 index shed 1.32 points to 69.21.
